articleBody: Custom second-story additions and major home expansions in Los Angeles County must be evaluated carefully for **structural capacity, seismic performance, and code compliance**. The California Residential Code establishes structural design criteria, including load paths, lateral bracing, and connections. When adding a second story, structural engineers typically assess whether the existing foundation and framing can support additional loads and meet current seismic standards. In many cases, the California Existing Building Code provides methodologies for strengthening older structures while accommodating additions. Los Angeles is in a high seismic risk region, and building departments rely on seismic design parameters set by the California Building Code, which references standards from organizations like the Structural Engineers Association of California. For older homes, especially those built before modern seismic codes, additions often trigger upgrades such as foundation bolting, cripple wall bracing, and improved connections between floors and roof structures. City policies may also interact with soft-story retrofit ordinances for multi-unit buildings, though single-family homes are typically addressed through standard building code requirements during permit review. Zoning rules administered by the Los Angeles Department of City Planning influence what expansions are allowed. Height limits, floor area ratio (FAR), and neighborhood-specific ordinances like the Baseline Mansionization Ordinance can cap the total size and bulk of the expanded home. Setbacks and daylight-plane or articulation rules may shape second-story massing to reduce impacts on neighbors. Additions must also meet the California Energy Code, which can require upgrades to insulation, fenestration, and HVAC systems beyond the new area alone. Building and safety departments often require full plan sets, including structural calculations, energy compliance documentation, and detailed architectural drawings, and they may require multiple inspections to confirm that the existing structure and new work function as an integrated, code-compliant system.
